description.narrative: The development objective of the Digital Acceleration Project for Rwanda is to increase access to broadband and selected digital public services and strengthen the digital innovation ecosystem. The project comprises of four components. The first component, digital access and inclusion will increase digital access and inclusion through investment in digital access enablers, focusing on under-served areas and groups. It consists of following sub-components: (i) access to affordable smart devices; (ii) digital literacy for all; (iii) last mile connectivity access; and (iv) legal, regulatory, and institutional capacity for broadband market development. The second component, digital public service delivery will strengthen the Government of Rwanda (GoR's) ability to securely deliver more digital services, allowing for increased resilience and adaptability to health, climate, and other shocks. It consists of following sub-components: (i) digital identification and authentication; (ii) government data management, sharing, and analytics; (iii) e-services in key sectors; and (iv) cybersecurity resilience and data protection. The third component, digital innovation and entrepreneurship will strengthen the local digital entrepreneurship ecosystem and talent base. It consists of following sub-components: (i) regional digital entrepreneurship hub; and (ii) next generation capabilities for the digital economy. The fourth component, project management will finance project management costs associated with administering the project, including core project management functions related to financial management (FM), procurement, monitoring and evaluation (M and E), environmental and social framework (ESF) compliance, as well as project communications and coordination.
To increase access to broadband and selected digital public services, and strengthen the digital innovation ecosystem

title.narrative: New e-waste collection centers established and managed

comment.narrative:
Progress on track. 21 out of 30 planned collection points now established. Establishment of remaining 9 centers are in progress, and thus expect by project closing.
Enviroserve has collected some 233.67 tons of e-waste through these collection points nationwide. Awareness campaigns and training sessions on e-waste management have also been completed, supported by incentives provided to e-waste pickers operating across the country. To date, 140 e-waste pickers have been trained and supplied with personal protective equipment for safe collection. Additionally, 16 collection agents were recruited and trained to maintain the established collection points.

comment.narrative:
Enrollment is due to begin in Aug 2025, targeting the enrollment of at least 20% of the population by Dec 2025, and a further 25-30% per semester in 2026, placing the project on track to meet the target by closing.
The target is based on the total population estimated by 2026 which is expected to be roughly 14 million. 75% would thus be equivalent to 10.5 million.

title.narrative: People issued and actively using digital ID credentials

comment.narrative: ID credential issuance is expected to start in early 2026, based on the first round of enrollment conducted at the end of 2025, which would allow for subsequent ID verification (usage). Because there is lag between enrollment, credential issues and subsequent usage the target is lower then for the proposed enrollment target based on what can realistically be registered by project closing. However, credential issuance is expected to continue well beyond the closing date on the back of enrollment and systems investments made by the project.

title.narrative: Population enrolled in new digital ID system

comment.narrative:
Progress on track. Mass enrollment in the new digital ID system began in October 2025, following initial testing, deployment of registration kits, development of pre-enrollment and registration systems. Enrollment began in Gisagara, Huye, and Nyanza. To date, approximately 1.67% of the population has been registered. However, based on strong public turnout, supported by a targeted communications campaign, and the average processing time recorded, NIDA is on track to meet its enrollment targets.
The target is based on the total population estimated by 2026 which is expected to be roughly 14 million. 75% would thus be equivalent to 10.5 million.

title.narrative: Startups receiving funding through the project

comment.narrative: Progress on track. Hanga Venture Ignite was launched in February 2025. 259 startups applied. A first cohort of 22 companies are benefitting from early-stage financing support (15 ignite+, 7 ignite) across diverse sectors including FinTech (5), ClimateTech (3), HealthTech (4), AgTech (2), Mobility (2), and Logistics (1) and AI/ML (4). Another cohort 5 is currently in screening, with approximately 20 additional companies targeted for funding by year-end to fully commit remainder of funds, placing BRD on track to meet the target for financed start-ups.
